executive_brief: The Football Match Manager is a web-based tracking platform enabling users to browse, filter, and follow football matches in real-time. The system acts as a data aggregator, consuming third-party sports APIs to persist match states and user-specific interest mappings. Its core value lies in delivering high-freshness score updates and a personalized 'followed matches' experience for authenticated users.

architectural_constraints: Upcoming match data refresh interval: minimum every 6 hours
Live score update frequency: minimum every 1 minute during active matches
Final score update latency: maximum 5 minutes post-match completion
Match list load time: < 2 seconds for 95% of requests (cached)
Detail page load time: < 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests
Push notifications: Strictly out-of-scope for MVP
Social features and predictive analytics: Strictly out-of-scope for MVP
Responsive design requirement: Mandatory support for mobile and desktop

maturity_assessment: The specification is logically sound regarding user journeys but lacks a strategic foundation. The absence of a 'Goals & Objectives' section represents a critical structural gap that hinders the alignment of success KPIs with business value. While the functional requirements are granular, the project requires REFINEMENT to resolve uncertainties regarding the specific API provider and the final authentication protocol before execution.
critical_dependencies: External Football Data API (Mandatory for match schedules, live scores, and team/league metadata)
Third-party Authentication Provider (Google, Facebook, or Apple for user session persistence)
UserFollow entity: Strict relational join dependency between User and Match entities
Referential integrity: UserFollow records must depend on existing User and Match IDs
